summary: Across 2014 and 2023 Instagram posts, Olivia Chow positions small business support as central to job creation and local economic strength in Toronto. Chow advocates fixing the CaféTO program by shortening timelines, reducing costs, and creating more certainty for restaurants, and links small business health to fighting unemployment, expanding training and apprenticeships, and creating jobs for young people. Chow expresses support for fairness in the taxi industry, local journalism, the arts and film sector, and affordability for artists. Chow also backs community land trusts as a foundation for local economies and endorsed a $15/hour federal minimum wage in 2015. Specific actions cited include releasing a job creation and business platform (2014), touring the Orlando Training Centre as a model, meeting with taxi drivers, and challenging proposals to relocate 5,000 jobs out of Toronto.

key_positions.stance: Supports fixing CaféTO by shortening timelines, reducing costs, and creating more certainty for small businesses.
Supports small businesses as a key lever for fighting unemployment and creating jobs.
Supports expanding training and apprenticeships, citing the Orlando Training Centre as a model.
Supports community land trusts as a basis for strong local economies.
Supports fairness for taxi drivers in Toronto.
Supports affordability for artists and the importance of arts and film to Toronto's economy.
Opposes relocating 5,000 jobs out of Toronto.

key_actions.action: Released the first planks of a job creation and business platform focused on supporting small businesses.
Toured the Orlando Training Centre, citing it as a model for expanding training and apprenticeships.
Spoke to media questioning John Tory about relocating 5,000 jobs out of Toronto.
Met with taxi drivers from across Toronto to discuss fairness in their industry.
Pledged as mayor to fix CaféTO by shortening timelines, reducing costs, and creating more certainty.
